title: Fake news, influencers and health-related professional participation on the Web: A pilot study on a social-network of people with Multiple Sclerosis
screen_reason: Census content analysis of all 1,800 posts on the public wall of an Italian medically supervised Multiple Sclerosis patient network (April-June 2015). Two blinded experts classified 380 posts as having medical content and, within those, 72 as fake news and 308 as scientifically correct. Verbatim counts with stated denominators give a share of items classified false = CONTENT.

estimates.platform: SMsocialnetwork.com (Italian medically supervised social network for people with Multiple Sclerosis), public wall
estimates.measure_type: % of medical-content posts on the community's public wall classified as fake news
estimates.value_raw: 72 fake-news posts of 380 posts with medical content ("Among them, 308 reported scientific and relevant medical information, whereas 72 posts included fake news") = 18.9%
estimates.denominator: 380 posts with scientific/medical content on the SMsocialnetwork public wall, April-June 2015 (out of 1,800 posts collected; the remaining 1,420 were general interest)
estimates.definition: "any post including information that did not reflect a scientific truth or partially including scientifically based information that might have generated possible misinterpretation, was appointed as 'fake news'" - i.e. both outright untrue claims and partially correct claims liable to be misinterpreted.
estimates.misinfo_def: "fake news i.e. deceiving stories containing partial truths or stories that are speculative and not based on evidence" (Introduction), operationalised as above.
estimates.source_quote: We collected 1800 posts from the SMsocialnetwork public wall. Among these, the two experts identified 380 posts with medical content (126 posts per month, on average). Among them, 308 reported scientific and relevant medical information, whereas 72 posts included fake news. The remaining 1420 posts were of general interest, such as movies, the weather, music, walks, travels etc.
estimates.page_loc: Results, section 3, p. 176 (also in the Abstract)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: "two experts (one neurologist and one psychologist with specific MS knowledge) classified the posts"; the experts were blind to the users/authors of the posts; no inter-rater agreement statistic, no adjudication procedure and no codebook beyond the one-sentence criterion are reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: In the first part of the study, we collected the posts published on the public wall of SMsocialnetwork from April to June 2015 and two experts (one neurologist and one psychologist with specific MS knowledge) classified the posts into those with scientific or medical content, and those concerning social interactions or of general interest. The two experts were blind to the users/authors of the posts.
estimates.notes: 72/380 = 18.9% (exact part/whole from two verbatim counts, R8-compliant; the percentage itself is not printed in the paper). denom_selection=single_source because the corpus is the entire public wall of ONE small community website whose medical information flow is actively supervised by neurologists and psychologists - the authors' own thesis is that this supervision suppressed fake news, so the estimate is not transferable to unsupervised platforms. population_scope 'other' = a clinical patient community (people with MS) plus the supervising clinicians, not the general public. quote_verbatim=false: the source_quote is the sentence in READING ORDER; the two-column layout rendering of this PDF interleaves the left and right columns line by line, so the sentence is not a single contiguous span in the extracted text file and no reading-order rendering exists for this paper.

General-interest posts (movies, weather, music, travel) are in the denominator but cannot be in the numerator.

estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same two blinded experts (neurologist + psychologist with MS expertise); no reliability statistic reported.

The two rows are alternative denominators for one finding and must NOT both enter a pooled analysis - pick 18.9% for 'share of health-topic content' or 4.0% for 'share of all platform content'. definition_variant flagged true only to mark the pairing; strictly the difference is the DENOMINATOR, not the misinformation definition (the schema has no denominator-variant flag). 72/1800 = 4.0%, exact part/whole from verbatim counts. quote_verbatim=false: the source_quote is the sentence in READING ORDER; the two-column layout rendering of this PDF interleaves the left and right columns line by line, so the sentence is not a single contiguous span in the extracted text file and no reading-order rendering exists for this paper.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The influencer analysis is not a prevalence estimate and was not extracted: "Four of the six appointed AU had written only posts with relevant medical information and never fake news" (4/6 influencers), and the two remaining influencers posted only general-interest content (they had published 270 and 480 posts). This is a share of influencers, not a share of items or of people exposed. (2) Survey descriptives are not misinformation measures: 130 questionnaires completed (31% male, 69% female), 35.6% excluded for >20% missing data, 1,020 active users in the window, average 47 posts per active user. (3) No exposure, reach or sharing measure exists in the paper: post-level view or share counts are never reported, so nothing can be said about how many users saw the 72 fake-news posts. (4) Judgement call: the fake-news definition explicitly includes partially correct information liable to be misinterpreted, so breadth is coded 'misleading' rather than 'false'; a stricter reading would place this near the QUALITY boundary, but the label is an explicit veracity judgement against scientific truth, so CONTENT stands. (5) Setting caveat for the adjudicator: this platform was purpose-built by neurologists and psychologists who moderate medical information and explain to users why a post is fake news, so both estimates are from an actively debunked environment - the authors present the low figure as evidence of a "web safe environment".

rob.design: Cross-sectional census content analysis plus a community questionnaire. Frame: all posts on the public wall of SMsocialnetwork.com (a single Italian MS patient community with 1,020 active users) from April to June 2015, n = 1,800 posts. Classification by two experts - one neurologist and one psychologist with specific MS knowledge - blinded to post authorship; two-stage scheme (medical vs general interest, then correct vs fake news); NO inter-coder reliability statistic, no third adjudicator, no published codebook. Second part: two-item questionnaire fielded July-August 2015, 130 completed (31% male, 69% female), 35.6% discarded for >20% missing data (self-selected, one response per user, users blind to other responses); no denominator for a response rate is given against the 1,020 active users. Ethics approved (University of Campania Luigi Vanvitelli), no funding. Authors' own stated limits: high questionnaire missingness, no unsupervised comparison network exists, and results may not generalise beyond an MS-specific supervised network.
